founder.name: Frederick Charles L. Castro
bioParagraphs: Hello! I’m Frederick Charles L. Castro, but you can call me Chogs. Over the last decade, I’ve dedicated my life to building sustainable solutions for communities facing acute clean water shortages and educational barriers.
My philosophy is simple: non-profit work shouldn’t just be charity; it should be direct empowerment. We build local capacity so communities can thrive independently.
founder.quote: Real change happens when we stop treating beneficiaries as passive recipients and start treating them as leaders of their own future.

milestones.title: The Spark of Hope
milestones.description: Started as a small community initiative after witnessing severe resource inequality during a volunteer trip abroad.

milestones.title: Official Non-Profit Registration
milestones.description: Incorporated 501(c)(3) status and launched our flagship clean water accessibility program.

milestones.title: Expanding to Tech & Education
milestones.description: Partnered with global tech companies to bring computer literacy to over 20 underfunded school districts.

milestones.title: $1M+ Raised & 15k+ Lives Impacted
milestones.description: Achieved major milestone through sustainable community partnerships and transparent donor accountability.

items.name: Radical Transparency
items.desc: Open financial reporting and direct tracking for every dollar donated.

items.name: Empathy-Driven Action
items.desc: Listening first to community needs before building sustainable solutions.

items.name: Long-Term Sustainability
items.desc: Creating local capacity so projects remain self-sufficient after launch.

items.name: Global Collaboration
items.desc: Uniting donors, local leaders, and experts across borders.
